items.headline: Building advertising for the way people use AI
items.summary: OpenAI's own announcement of a new ChatGPT ad format and measurement stack — the primary source for this week's biggest AI-advertising story.
items.notes: og:image unobtainable from openai.com (JS-rendered, no OG tags); fallback is OpenAI's own announcement asset as rehosted by TechCrunch. Same story cluster as items 2-5.

items.headline: OpenAI moves to make ChatGPT Ads more measurable — and more visual
items.summary: OpenAI answers advertiser complaints with a new ad format, measurement tooling and brand-suitability testing inside ChatGPT Ads.
items.notes: Buy-side read on the OpenAI announcement: measurement and format detail.

items.headline: OpenAI Is Piloting Brand Suitability Controls With DoubleVerify and IAS
items.summary: DoubleVerify and IAS will independently assess how ChatGPT applies brand-safety standards in a sandbox, and OpenAI adds Negative Phrases placement exclusions for brands.
items.notes: Distinct reportable fact from items 1-2: third-party verification and brand-suitability controls for ads in a chat surface.

items.headline: OpenAI To Test Visual Ads In ChatGPT Image Generation
items.summary: ChatGPT Ads will test visual ads during image generation in the U.S. as OpenAI expands measurement partners — written for PPC teams deciding what to evaluate and track.
items.notes: Practitioner angle on the new visual ad format; paid-placement story, not organic SEO.

items.headline: OpenAI launches visual ads that appear alongside image generation results
items.summary: The new ads will appear later this month in the U.S. only, featuring products and services from an initial test group of advertisers.
items.notes: Same visual-ads story as item 4, from a general-tech outlet.

items.headline: TikTok Unveils AI-Powered Updates for Advertisers: Driving Discovery, Action, and Measurable Business Outcomes
items.summary: TikTok's Advertising Week announcement: agentic commerce with Buy Direct and a conversational Shopping Assistant, Smart+-powered Search Ads campaigns and Smart+ Creative Selection.
items.notes: Primary source for the TikTok cluster (items 7-9). published time read from the embedded publishedDate field (2026-10-05T22:19:56.418Z), not a snippet.

items.headline: TikTok broadens agentic AI play, brings global ad network to US
items.summary: Products timed to Advertising Week extend TikTok's agentic ad automation and open its off-platform ad network to U.S. buyers ahead of the holidays.
items.notes: Buying-side framing of the TikTok announcement.

items.headline: TikTok's ad network bet: More reach, more budget
items.summary: TikTok wants a bigger share of advertiser budgets by selling inventory beyond its own app, with agentic buying attached.

items.headline: TikTok Expands Its Off-Platform Ad Network to US Advertisers
items.summary: The rebranded Pangle network spans nearly 400,000 apps, and TikTok will let advertisers launch and run TikTok campaigns from AI tools like Claude and Perplexity.
items.notes: Media buying moving into third-party AI assistants is the distinct fact here. Replaces the dropped Adweek TikTok shopping-assistant piece under the 3-per-outlet cap.

items.headline: ADWEEK Tech Advantage: AI Agents Are Increasingly Getting Their Hands on Ad Dollars
items.summary: As AI moves from making ads to making media decisions, the industry is arguing over how much spending authority agents get and who sets the rules.
items.notes: Agentic media buying: who controls the budget.

items.headline: Who Eats The Gap When Agentic Spend Outpaces Proof Of Impact?
items.summary: An AI agent can stay inside its budget and still spend too much, and proof of campaign performance arrives after the money is already committed.
items.notes: Agentic buying vs. measurement lag. Both halves pass squarely: the overspend only exists because an agent is doing the buying.

items.headline: AI Agents Are Coming For CTV; It's Cheaper For Politicians To Buy National Ads Than To Target Texas
items.summary: Custom buying agents from NBCUniversal, FreeWheel, Dentsu's Carat and Newton pair identity data with audience intelligence to recommend NBCU streaming inventory against an advertiser's desired outcome.
items.notes: Format caveat: this is a daily roundup, so a writer would need to work from the lead item (the NBCU/FreeWheel/Carat/Newton agentic CTV buying launch), which no other fresh item in the pool covers. Content passes both halves.

items.headline: Want an AI-Built MMM You Can Trust? Start With a Thesis
items.summary: M Squared's Madan Bharadwaj on why AI-generated marketing mix models make expert judgment matter more, not less, when you are allocating media budget.
items.notes: Measurement/MMM — the in-scope axis that decides where ad money goes.

items.headline: Omnicom Media and Rembrand partner to evolve in-content ad placements
items.summary: The holdco and the ad-tech platform push in-content ad insertion further, using AI to identify scenes that can be monetized contextually.
items.notes: New ad inventory created by AI scene detection. Replaces the dropped Digiday Media Agency Report under the 3-per-outlet cap.

items.headline: Pricing tactics come under scrutiny in the age of AI
items.summary: Concern that retailers are using customer data for AI-driven dynamic and personalized pricing is putting brands on the defensive about a core selling lever.
items.notes: Pricing/promotion as a selling lever, AI-driven.

items.headline: Gap unveils AI-assisted shopping, three decades after its first website
items.summary: Gap Inc. puts conversational shopping agents and the Alta Daily and Daydream recommendation platforms in front of customers across Gap, Banana Republic and Old Navy.
items.notes: AI at the point of conversion for a major retailer. Published time field carries no timezone (Industry Dive emits ET); 11:01 ET recorded as 15:01Z.
